spoken_text: Please walk me through one specific disruption, failover, recovery test, or operational recovery in the last 36 months where you used an external recovery platform or managed recovery service. Start wherever the event became your problem, and tell me what happened in as much detail as you can.
In that event, who actually moved what got restored first — or who could have stopped it?

spoken_text: What gave that person or group the ability to move the decision — their position, a written rule, the clock, something else?
If that pull had not been there, what would you have done differently?
In that event, whose request or pressure most affected what got restored first?
Was there anyone who could delay, override, or stop a recovery action you thought was right?
If that pressure had not been there, what would you have done differently?
Whose claim to a service or a recovery order did people treat as having a right to ask for it?
Was anyone’s request treated as out of line or outside their role? What happened then?
What made one service or one stakeholder more time-critical than another in that event?
Did that sense of time pressure change while you were working the incident? What changed it?
Who was supposed to make the call on that tradeoff, and who actually made it?
Was there a moment when you needed authority you did not have? What did you do?
What, if anything, triggered an escalation?
